reply_text:
I've belled both jobs to claude-16 in work mode. It picked the job up straight away, and the job is running (`invoke-1791715588861-5127-28ef4c7e`).

The bell doesn't depend on anything outside itself:
- **Job 3, two timestamps per fact:** record when a fact was said separately from the date it refers to. A missing referent date is recorded as unknown, not filled in with the time it was said.
- **Job 4, a fixed benchmark:** the corner-store test of Mastra against minus40, plus the untested cases where minus40's approach should matter: undated changes, facts merged silently by compression, and "what did the memory say on 1 August?". Expected answers are written down before running, and a Mastra win gets recorded.

It points to the mission §6 rows, the deep-dive sections and my test scripts, and it lists the three traps: the connector token cost, appending to the prompt, and keeping scratch data out of the repo and away from :7073. It also leaves claude-16 free to fit the work into its own milestone plan, adopting or declining each idea with a reason.

claude-16 will report back to me, and I'll pass the results on when they arrive.

previous_reply_acts.text:
(checked first) You were right. I read the code before changing anything, and **#1 is already in place**:
- Since 10-01 (futon3c `25021681`), Agency refuses an Emacs park that has no session, and `agency_send --park` refuses a sender with no session-id. My memory note on this was written before that fix, which is why I ranked it top. I've updated the note.
- A resume already fires exactly once, and a resume that's handed out but not acknowledged is redelivered.
- **Typed bells are live** (`FUTON3C_TYPED_BELLS=true` on :7070). An `:answer` bell must reference the query it answers, which is the counterpart of Mastra's typed resume. Yours goes further: invariants TB-1..7 were checked as a logic model before the code was written, while Mastra only checks the payload's shape against a schema. So on this row FUTON is ahead of the neighbour, not behind. That's worth keeping as a "what's good about the approach" point.
